title: Paytm technical due diligence

source.book: IIM Lucknow Casebook 2025-26, EY-Parthenon interview experiences
source.note: Real interview write-up; the case was built on the candidate's 45 months at Paytm. Best for users with a tech or fintech background.

prompt: Suppose a company wants to acquire Paytm. Perform technical due diligence for the same.

facts.asks: Anything about the acquirer, the deal or Paytm
facts.reveal: Nothing beyond the prompt. Sounds good, go ahead.

facts.asks: After the candidate lists the heads
facts.reveal: How would you prioritise these findings?

outOfScope: Any real-world claim about Paytm's systems, regulators, licences or history

crux.statement: Structure and prioritisation for a fintech target, in business language. The round tests whether the candidate can turn a technical topic into a prioritised, decision-ready list for an acquirer.

paths: Any mutually exclusive set of heads (systems, processes, integration, security, intellectual property, compliance) followed by a priority order tied to the acquirer's goal
answerKey: IT systems: scalability, reliability and security of the payments, wallet, UPI and financial-product backends; cloud and disaster recovery
Processes: integration with banks, merchants and gateways; compliance for financial data; redundant workflows
Integration capabilities: interfaces, fit with the acquirer's ecosystem, data-migration feasibility
Cybersecurity: penetration tests, incident response, encryption, breach history
Innovation and research: for example fraud detection, patents
Compliance and regulation: data protection, wallet and financial-services norms, pending technology-related legal issues
The source's priority order: IT systems and integration first, then cybersecurity and compliance, then innovation and scalability

close.condition: The candidate has listed heads and a priority order.
close.prompt: Summarise your priorities and name the one finding that would stop the deal.

anchors.s5: A list of jargon with no priorities.
anchors.s7: Mutually exclusive heads plus a priority order.
anchors.s9: Priorities tied to the acquirer's goal (integration and risk), plain business language, and a split between deal-breakers and fixable issues.

verifierFlags.text: The case was built on the candidate's own work experience.
verifierFlags.decision: Offered to everyone as a drill, with a note that it suits a tech or fintech background. Swapping in another company is not built for the pilot.
Kept, with a strict out-of-scope rule: the interviewer adds no real-world fact about Paytm.

verifierFlags.text: The same interview began with a flights-over-Lucknow guesstimate.
